free_variables.meaning: result of stat() on the fixed path 'C:/Program Files/AMD/ROCm' at call time

encoding.reduction_notes: defaultPath is the module constant DEFAULT_ROCM_BIN_PATH_WINDOWS = Path('C:/Program Files/AMD/ROCm'). The argument string is fully constant; Path(const).exists() therefore reduces to a single filesystem boolean probe with NO public-input, CLI, YAML, env, or arithmetic dependency. z3 over this single free boolean is trivially SAT for both polarities, which is not a real solve of any input space -- hence solver_status=unknown (the witnesses are runtime/filesystem state, given by value, not solver-derived from inputs).

z3_run.note: Trivially SAT: the only free variable is external filesystem state, so SAT here does not constitute a public-input solve.

runtime_probe.note: On this Linux container the path does not exist (False). On a Windows host with ROCm installed at the default location it would be True. The enclosing _windowsSearchPaths is only invoked on Windows (callers gate on os.name == 'nt').

true_examples.how: Windows host with ROCm installed at the default location -> directory exists -> exists() is True; _windowsLatestRocmBin(defaultPath) is then probed for X.Y subdirs.

false_examples.how: Any host where 'C:/Program Files/AMD/ROCm' does not exist (every Linux/macOS box, and Windows without a default-location ROCm install) -> exists() is False -> the default-ROCm-bin search branch is skipped.

pure_helper_notes: No pure helper can be extracted: the branch condition is exclusively a side-effecting filesystem stat on a hardcoded path. There are no boolean/integer/comparison public inputs to fold into a deterministic predicate function, so CrossHair is not applicable.
notes: Add-only deliverable analysis; no repo files modified. The witnesses are filesystem-state values, not solver-proven over inputs; both polarities are reachable purely by toggling whether the constant Windows ROCm path exists on disk.
